evidence.locator: Session management; Export a session; Projects; Worktree branches; Keyboard shortcuts; Find a session by name; Install as an app; Open in VS Code or Cursor
evidence.finding: Sessions persist across browser refreshes and server restarts; Clone session forks to another agent. Export downloads <session-id>.jsonl (session metadata plus every committed item), the same format as omnigent session export and importable with omnigent session import; a failure shows an Export failed toast. Projects group sessions in non-nesting sidebar folders with per-project defaults; deleting a project archives its sessions. The composer can name a worktree branch and base, and Settings > Git can always use a random worktree. Cmd/Ctrl+/ opens a shortcuts overlay; Cmd+Opt+S (Ctrl+Alt+S) opens a name-only fuzzy session switcher and Cmd+K a palette that searches sessions. The Files panel can open a file in VS Code or Cursor. evidence.locator: GitHub; Tracked pull requests; Summary tab; When the host is offline; GitLab merge requests
evidence.finding: Coding-agent sessions have a Pull Requests tab listing PRs found from the agent's gh and GitHub MCP actions or linked manually. Rows show passed, pending and failed CI check counts (hover lists the checks) and refresh about every 30 seconds; the Summary tab shows reviewers with review states, CI checks and the description. For GitHub PRs users can edit title and description, labels, request or withdraw reviewers, post comments and replies, and merge after confirming a method; these need edit access to the session and run as the host's gh account. While the host is offline, rows show stored title and status and live checks and merge return when it reconnects. GitLab merge requests (via glab or a token) and Azure DevOps pull requests are read-only. On a phone the tab opens in a drawer.

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Web UI, inline comments and Inbox
evidence.locator: Inline comments and addressing; Inbox; Reply from the Inbox
evidence.finding: Users click a passage in a file or the agent's output and leave an inline comment; the comments panel separates Open and Sent comments and Address All sends every open comment to the agent in one message for revision, for example when reviewing a plan before execution. The Inbox lists pending approval requests to answer in place and sessions with unread agent output, filtered by All, Unread and Awaiting response; users with edit access can reply from a card.

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Web UI, scheduled tasks
evidence.locator: Scheduled tasks; Starting from a template; Failed runs; Trigger templates; PagerDuty; Change events; One task session for every trigger match
evidence.finding: Automations run a saved prompt on a recurrence on a connected host or a fresh managed sandbox. Trigger templates for Jira, Slack, GitHub, Linear and PagerDuty start one session per newly matching item (at most 10 per run) and can post the link back; they poll and do not receive webhooks, every 10 minutes by default with automations v2 or hourly otherwise, and need the service's MCP server or the gh CLI where the task runs. A failed run marks the task card and, if no session started, appears in the Inbox as Automation failed with the reason; dismissing it does not rerun the task.

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Scheduled Tasks
evidence.locator: Where a task runs (connected_host, managed_sandbox); How a firing runs: scheduling guarantees
evidence.finding: The server database is the scheduler's source of truth and re-arms active tasks on start. A connected_host task runs on a pinned or the most recently active online host; if none is live the occurrence is recorded as a failed run (host_offline). A managed_sandbox task provisions a fresh server-managed sandbox for each firing and requires a configured sandbox provider. Missed fires are not replayed (no backfill after downtime) and an occurrence that arrives while the previous run is in flight is dropped.

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Cloud Sandbox Host
evidence.locator: Introduction and provider comparison; Server-managed; How long a sandbox stays warm; Run automations in sandboxes; Build a provider plugin
evidence.finding: A cloud sandbox host moves the runner from the laptop to a remote container on Databricks Sandbox, Modal, Daytona, Blaxel, Islo, Gensee, NVIDIA OpenShell, Boxlite or AWS Lambda MicroVMs; it keeps running when the laptop closes, while a local runner stops. evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Pair Programming
evidence.locator: Co-drive; What each permission level can do; Only the owner can change the agent; Fork; Fork onto a cloud sandbox
evidence.finding: Owners share a session with Read or Edit access; Edit collaborators send messages that execute on the owner's host through the same policy gates. Changing permission mode or launch args, transferring terminals, browsing absolute host paths and the raw environment shell stay owner-only and are enforced by the server (PATCH /v1/sessions and a 403 on the shell endpoint). evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Auth & SSO

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Programmatic Usage
evidence.locator: Before you start; Start a session; Let an agent manage other sessions (tool table)
evidence.finding: The omnigent-client package (or the full omnigent package) provides the Python omnigent_client SDK, whose version should match the server. Agent tools include sys_session_create (child session), sys_session_send (follow-up to a direct child, or reuse of a named sub-agent), sys_session_message (other sessions of the same user), sys_session_list, sys_session_get_info and sys_session_get_history (read another session's recent messages and tool results).

evidence.title: Omnigent docs: Omnibox
evidence.locator: Filesystem isolation; Network isolation; Credential injection
evidence.finding: Omnibox wraps an agent in an OS sandbox (bubblewrap and seccomp on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS).
